# Actual public coverage-command profile

SOURCE ONLY: no syntax check, constructor injection, native call or build has
run for this driver. It is a diagnostic on the same small coverage-cost problem,
not another production strategy or performance qualification.

`adapter/profile-reference-coverage-command.mjs` runs one fresh child process
and owned database per selected role/case. It imports the immutable recipe and
EventOracle from the existing cost fixture only after all four cost source
files match Git `cf7f0d86645383944cac77c2f49e331428c75a33`. It reuses
`patch-profile-sql.mjs` only to decode the observed operator tree. There is no
copied benchmark loop, generated result, SQL replacement or optimizer change.

The exact2f/source467 versus a562/source229 pair and unchanged SDK19c/engine72
are fixed by the same role constants as the cost screen. Native/SDK entry files,
core source maps, matching owner/writer sources, source Git objects and actual
selected engine resolution are pinned before/after. All four cost dependency
files are checked again after the child. No native emitter binary is built:
the actual production-expanded SQL text is observed directly in each native
JSON profile's `query.sql`.

Each selected case uses the exact zero-noise recipe, schema, seed batches,
four warmups and first measured request from the cost screen. Seed receipts
areK2/K3, warmupsK4..K7, and the profiled `measure-4` patch writes integer5 on
TargetA in `[20,80)` atK8. Ordinary retained defaults are unchanged:1,000,000
facts and268,435,456 bytes. The selected native header declares those defaults;
1MiB is the new logical coverage-proof cap, not the retained-store budget.

A diagnostic-only descriptor wrapper calls the ORIGINAL selected
DuckDBInstance.create once, adding only this creation configuration:

```text
allowed_configs=['enable_profiling','profiling_coverage','profiling_output']
```

The constructor descriptor is restored immediately after normal store open.
All existing configuration locks remain active; only these three profiler
settings may change. Memory128MB/temp64MB/threads4/readers1/UV4 and public
scheduling are untouched. The actual captured writer port configures its
actual worker through the original runWriter, checking lock=true, JSON, ALL
and an empty output path. The store's one original patch call and real native
PRAGMA remain unchanged. No SQL is split, reordered, interleaved or replaced.
The observation wrapper returns the original result and records the one actual
call plus its existing metrics. It never manufactures dispatch, receipt or ACK.

Pinned source supports this hypothesis: client_context_execution.cpp539–546
calls QueryProfiler.EndQuery between expanded statements, independently of
registered owner QueryEnd at143–146. With empty profiling_output,
QueryProfiler.cpp224–260 prints; JSONTreeRenderer103–106 emits full native JSON
and PrinterTreeRenderer defaults to STDERR. ALL makes every physical operator
eligible. This is source proof for a candidate capture mechanism; actual profile
coverage still must pass the executable gate.

Synchronous unique FD2 markers bracket ONE actual public patch. The parent
drains/copies stdout and stderr without modifying them, then parses concatenated
JSON only between those markers. A string/escape-aware JSON scanner handles
braces inside SQL literals. It requires more than20 observed statements, exact
owner-guard prefix, a positive actual CTAS operator, main.clock mutation and
final receipt query associated with measure-4. Raw profiles are saved separately
with hashes and native query/parser/planner/optimizer/storage/system fields.
Settings-only, last-receipt-only, truncated or unassociated output is a failed
first capture, not silently replaced with a different query or trace route.

Exact old/current typed points and presence, semantic property history, full
receipt replay, six selected native images, all five cleanup zeros and closed
no-WAL database are verified. Failed setup/capture/native/result/identity
outcomes remain preserved. No retry, cap increase or alternate raw-SQL execution
is attempted. Each selected invocation is one separately granted attempt.

After source review and an exclusive lease, first syntax check; then invoke one
case with a fresh ABSENT output directory (example baseline):

```sh
env UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE=4 NODE_OPTIONS= node adapter/profile-reference-coverage-command.mjs \
  --role baseline --scenario zero \
  --runtime __HANDOFF_ROOT__/duckdb-temporal/variants/temporal-presence-intervals-20261106/runtime \
  --cost-root __HANDOFF_ROOT__/duckdb-temporal/variants/temporal-native-writer-20261105/runtime \
  --output __HANDOFF_ROOT__/duckdb-temporal/variants/temporal-presence-intervals-qa-20261106/runtime/build/coverage-command-profile-20261106-01/baseline-zero
```

Candidate uses the matching coverage runtime and role candidate; zero,
unrelated and incoming cases are separately selected. Baseline accepts only
zero: it cannot parse schema5 and is never treated as an equivalent coverage
implementation. The parent output directory must exist; each case directory
must be absent. No original timed database or result is opened or modified.

Public wall includes profiler rendering/pipe pressure and is NOT service
latency. Query/planning/operator/native/public timers overlap, so do not sum or
subtract them into exclusive C++/DuckDB phases. EndQueryInternal commits before
its final profiler.EndQuery: the last receipt profile may include commit.
Retain any actual storage metrics, but do not invent a standalone commit time
or separate callback time. The task's stopping result is a concrete observed
statement/plan attribution or a preserved unsupported-capture outcome, not a
new benchmark framework or an optimization claim.
